packs.title: Streets to the Bay
packs.promise: Collect street textures, make small stories and meet the mainland waterfront.

q.s: Find a pattern without interrupting a game.
st: Choose a public-sidewalk viewpoint at the edge of the park, clear of players and entrances.
Look for a domino-themed paving detail, a repeated shade-support shape and a border between path and planting.
Record the three patterns and choose the one that most clearly separates a place to move from a place to stay.

q.s: Collect the texture around the color.
st: Stay on the public sidewalk outside gallery and attraction entrances.
Find three different surface treatments on public-facing walls or street fixtures: smooth, layered and weathered.
Describe how the same color would look different on each surface; no particular mural is required.

q.s: Find a line for water, people and plants.
st: Choose an open public baywalk section away from museum entrances and water edges.
Find three boundaries: where planting stops, where the walking surface changes and where the park meets the bay.
Describe one practical job each boundary performs.

packs.title: Pastel & Tides
packs.promise: Find a new alphabet in the architecture, then carry it to the water.

q.s: Collect three architectural shapes and give each a letter.
st: Begin at Ocean Drive and 10th Street. Choose the public sidewalk with the clearest view of the hotel facades, using marked crossings.
Look for a curve, a repeated geometric form, and a detail that reminds you of a ship. The last choice is your interpretation, not an architecture quiz.
Assign A, B, and C to your discoveries. Note the nearest street or a visible building name so you could find each again.
Choose which shape you would recognize with the color removed. Save your three discoveries and that choice.

q.s: Build the beginning of a film in three imagined shots.
st: Choose a clear paved viewpoint near 8th Street with a building edge, a palm, and some open sky in view.
Imagine three shots: one wide view to establish the place, one close detail, and one small movement such as a palm frond or passing cloud.
Give the sequence a one-sentence story premise of your own. Keep real people out of the cast unless a companion freely joins in.
Photograph one of the shots or describe all three in a field note. The imagined film is complete without video, performance, or public sharing.

q.s: Let a short trolley ride rearrange your picture of South Beach.
st: Go to the signed southbound stop at Washington Avenue and 9th Street. Check the live South Beach Loop A service and destination before boarding.
Ride toward Washington Avenue and 4th Street, requesting that stop in good time. While seated or securely holding a rail, notice one change in building scale, street color, and greenery.
After you have left the vehicle and cleared the boarding area, choose the change that most altered the mood of the street.
Save your three changes and chosen moment. If a ride is unavailable, the stationary alternative completes the same mission.
